request.spec:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each user can now choose which people-list columns their own screen shows, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What you see:** a row of checkboxes (`column-<name>`) sits just above the people list, all ticked to start. Unticking one removes that column from this user's screen entirely: both its header and its cell are gone. Totals, rollups, the header figures, the summary and other users' screens are unaffected. "excess" also has a checkbox, besides the 14 columns in the request, because the test switches it off too.

**How the choice is kept:**
- It's saved in the database per sheet and per user, so it survives re-loading the sheet. I stored it per sheet rather than once per user (the way locale is stored), because the tests reuse user names across sheets. One consequence: a user who hides a column on one sheet still sees it on their other sheets.
- Each click saves only the one column it changed. Saves go out one after another, and re-loading the sheet waits for them to finish, so quick clicks followed by a refresh can't bring back an old choice.
- Changing columns writes no audit line, since it only affects how one user's screen looks.

**What I changed:**
- **Database:** a new migration, `V73__user_columns.sql`, adds a `user_hidden_column` table. It's left out of sheet snapshots and as-of views, since it's a screen preference, not sheet data.
- **Server:** two new endpoints. `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/columns/{user}` returns the hidden columns. `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/columns/{user}/{column}` with `{shown}` switches one column on or off and refuses unknown column names. The classes are in `session/` (`ColumnsRepository`, `ValidateColumn`, `ApplyColumn`, etc.).
- **Front end:** the new code is in `features/columns/`. In each of the claims, rates, statements, overdue, patrons, hold, retire, aliases and people files, the header and data cell are now shown or hidden by the user's choice. Action cells, like the hold button, always stay.
